subject.title: Browser-heavy sessions block all main lanes — need dedicated browser lane or per-channel lane routing

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class browser/per-channel lane routing, fold this case into broader per-agent lane work, or solve it with a different foreground-fairness scheduler policy?
rationale: The queue primitives already accept custom lanes, but exposing lane routing changes public config, fairness guarantees, aggregate resource caps, and channel/workload trust boundaries.

options.title: Design lane-routing policy
options.body: Sponsor a bounded scheduler design that covers browser/channel/agent classification, aggregate caps, default compatibility, docs, and regression tests before code changes.

options.title: Fold into per-agent lanes
options.body: Treat this as a browser-heavy use case under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43235 unless per-agent isolation proves insufficient.

options.title: Prefer priority fairness
options.body: Avoid new lane config for now and instead pursue foreground reserve or priority-aging work that keeps fast user turns responsive on shared lanes.

recommendation.title: Design lane-routing policy
recommendation.body: Sponsor a bounded scheduler design that covers browser/channel/agent classification, aggregate caps, default compatibility, docs, and regression tests before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal ties the command-lane config boundary and prior review context to @steipete's history in this area.
